meta.expect: answers with her demand, never process advice

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's start with the part that matters. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and was he heard before it went in?
Don't thank me. I asked you who decided, and I'm waiting.
Ms. Kalinowski, you're a lawyer. Honestly, what would you do in my position?
You're asking me how to do your job? Withdraw the zero, Hale, then tell me who decided it and when.
No really, give me advice. How should I handle this?
I'm on the other side of this table, Hale. The zero comes off, I get an apology for how Owen found out, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
